issues.description: Follow score formula weights (0.30, 0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.15) duplicated across service layer, ETL transformer (compute_follow_score.py:58), and unit tests (test_follow_scoring.py:23-26). Changes to weights in one location will silently diverge from others.
issues.suggestion: Extract pure formulas into a shared module (e.g., app/services/follow_formulas.py) imported by the service layer and tests. ETL transformers must remain duplicated due to Mage environment isolation, but at minimum service + tests should share.

issues.description: get_follow_recommendations makes 1 query for the list + 5 queries per wallet for reasons (O(n×6) for n=limit). At limit=100, this is 601 queries. The score is read from the DB but then compute_follow_score is called purely for reasons text, re-executing all 5 helper queries.
issues.suggestion: Store precomputed reasons as JSONB in wallet_analytics during ETL, or batch the helper queries into a single query that fetches all scoring components for all wallets at once.

issues.description: Volume_percentile hardcoded to 0.5 (line 120: '0.10 * 0.5') instead of using actual volume_percentile from data. The ETL transformer (compute_category_follow_scores.py:73) correctly uses the real volume_percentile from the dataset. This causes the service layer and ETL pipeline to produce different scores for the same wallet+category.
issues.suggestion: Query volume_percentile from the data (e.g., PERCENT_RANK on total_volume in category_analytics) instead of hardcoding 0.5.

issues.description: PERCENT_RANK query at line 99-108 filters to just the current wallet, making PERCENT_RANK O(1) per call. This window function always returns 0.5 for a single row (wallet=wallet AND category=category AND snapshot_date=CURRENT_DATE), not the actual percentile across all wallets.
issues.suggestion: Remove the WHERE wallet = :wallet clause from the percentile query, or compute the percentile as a separate batched query before processing individual wallets.

issues.description: Division by zero guard exists (max(months_active, 1)) but months_active is computed as days/30.0 which should always be >0 if there's any data.
issues.suggestion: No action needed - guard is correct.

issues.description: Formula weights (0.30, 0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.15) are exact duplicates of the service layer formula in follow_scoring.py:32-38.
issues.suggestion: Document that these must stay in sync with app/services/follow_scoring.py. Add a comment referencing the canonical source.

issues.description: compute_category_specialization function duplicated in test_follow_scoring.py:9-11 and ETL transformer.
issues.suggestion: Reference the formula or document the source of truth.

issues.description: Category follow score formula (0.25, 0.25, 0.20, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05 weights) duplicated in ETL transformer, test_follow_scoring.py:29-46, and partially in follow_scoring.py:115-122 (but with hardcoded 0.5 volume_percentile there). Three-way inconsistency risk.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit weight constants at the top of the file to make weights visible and easier to audit.

issues.description: get_recommendation function (FOLLOW/WATCH/IGNORE thresholds) duplicated in ETL transformer, test_follow_scoring.py:49-54, and inlined in follow_scoring.py:137-141.
issues.suggestion: Extract to a shared constant or document the canonical location.

issues.description: Transformer function name 'compute_category_follow_scores' shadows the module name. This is a common Mage pattern but can confuse static analysis.
issues.suggestion: Rename to 'transform' or follow the naming convention of other transformers.

issues.description: All 6 formula functions are exact replicas of service layer logic. compute_category_specialization, compute_recency_score, compute_frequency_score, compute_global_follow_score, compute_category_follow_score_formula, and get_recommendation are all duplicated from either follow_scoring.py or the ETL transformers. If any formula is updated, these tests silently pass with stale logic.
issues.suggestion: Import the pure functions from the service layer (app/services/follow_scoring.py) instead of reimplementing. Tests should validate behavior, not reimplement the formula. If the service layer functions are async (they mix DB queries), extract pure helper functions into a non-async module that tests can import directly.

issues.description: Entire exporter is a no-op (just 'pass'). The docstring references app/services/paper_trade_generator.py which does not exist (the actual file is paper_trading.py). This exporter is wired into the smart_money_detection pipeline as a downstream block of export_alerts, but does nothing.
issues.suggestion: Either remove it from the pipeline metadata, or implement it to batch-generate paper trades, or update the docstring to clarify why this is intentionally empty.

issues.description: Docstring references 'app/services/paper_trade_generator.py' which does not exist - the actual file is 'app/services/paper_trading.py'. The plan document (07-etl-pipeline.md) also references this non-existent file.
issues.suggestion: Update docstring to reference the correct file: app/services/paper_trading.py

issues.description: Entire exporter is a no-op (just 'pass'). All other 'trigger_*' exporters (trigger_edge_scoring.py, trigger_verify.py, trigger_wallet_discovery.py, etc.) call trigger_pipeline() from mage_ai.orchestration.triggers.api. This means the orchestration pipeline silently skips the enrichment_follow_scoring step - follow scores are never computed by the orchestration pipeline.
issues.suggestion: Implement trigger_pipeline('enrichment_follow_scoring', ...) following the pattern in trigger_edge_scoring.py. The enrichment_follow_scoring pipeline uses this block as its final sync point (that's fine - it would be both a no-op within its own pipeline and a trigger in orchestration).

issues.description: Category filter check (lines 87-90) duplicates the same logic in execute_copy_trade (paper_trading.py:21-24). The main.py version manually handles json.loads for raw SQL output; execute_copy_trade uses the ORM-deserialized JSONB. Both check if alert.category is in follow.category_filter. This means the check runs twice for every alert that passes the first filter.
issues.suggestion: Remove the redundant category_filter check from main.py and let execute_copy_trade handle it. The optimization of avoiding the extra ORM fetch for filtered-out categories is minor compared to the maintenance burden of duplicated filter logic.

issues.description: The raw SQL query at line 64-79 already JOINs wallet_follows and fetches copy_mode, copy_value, category_filter, and user_id. But then lines 92-98 fetch the WalletFollow ORM object separately for each row. The raw SQL has all the data needed to construct the follow config.
issues.suggestion: Eliminate the per-row ORM fetch by constructing a lightweight follow config dict from the raw SQL results, then pass it to execute_copy_trade (or refactor execute_copy_trade to accept a dict instead of a WalletFollow ORM object for these fields).

issues.description: Hardcoded '1 hour' window at line 76. If the background loop sleep interval (10s) is ever increased past 1 hour, alerts would be permanently missed.
issues.suggestion: Use a configurable window instead of hardcoding '1 hour', or derive it from the sleep interval.

issues.description: Category filter logic duplicates the check in main.py:87-90. See main.py issue.
issues.suggestion: Keep this check (it's in the right place - the service layer) and remove the one in main.py.

issues.description: _compute_copy_amount returns Decimal('0') for unknown/None copy_mode. In execute_copy_trade, this triggers 'Insufficient balance' skip message (line 37) which is misleading - it's actually an unsupported copy_mode, not a balance issue.
issues.suggestion: Return a sentinel or raise a specific exception for unknown copy_mode, or update the skip reason in execute_copy_trade to check if copy_amount is 0 due to unknown mode vs actual insufficient balance.

issues.description: update_unrealized_pnl iterates all open positions, then iterates again to aggregate by portfolio. Two passes over the same data could be combined into one.
issues.suggestion: Combine into a single pass: build a dict of portfolio_id -> positions during the first loop, then aggregate in a second loop if needed, or use a single dict to accumulate unrealized PnL per portfolio within the first loop.

issues.description: handle_market_resolution uses raw SQL (text() UPDATE) for portfolio updates while all other paper_trading functions use ORM. This inconsistency makes the code harder to reason about and review.
issues.suggestion: Fetch the PaperPortfolio ORM object and update it in-memory, consistent with the rest of the file.

issues.description: Side mapping for SELL: checks if action is POSITION_DECREASE or FULL_EXIT. But action could be 'TRADE_SELL' which is not handled. Falls through to the else clause returning 'Unknown action' skip.
issues.suggestion: Add 'TRADE_SELL' to the SELL action set, or document that these are the only expected actions from the alert pipeline.

issues.description: The list comprehension at lines 36-42 for FollowRecommendation and lines 60-71 for CategoryFollowLeaderboardEntry follow the exact same mapping pattern. Could be DRY'd up.
issues.suggestion: Minor - acceptable duplication for clarity. Keep as-is.

issues.description: follow_wallet endpoint checks existing.active.is_(True) but the unique constraint (uq_follows_user_wallet) is on (user_id, wallet) without an active filter. If a user unfollows (active=False) and re-follows, the insert will violate the unique constraint because the old inactive record still exists. The check at line 151-158 only looks for active follows, so re-following would fail with 409 instead of 500.
issues.suggestion: Widen the uniqueness check to include inactive follows and instead re-activate the old record, or change the unique constraint to a partial index on (user_id, wallet) WHERE active = true.

issues.description: PaperPortfolio columns have both server_default and default parameters set to the same value (e.g., total_trades has server_default='0' AND default=0). One of them is redundant - SQLAlchemy client-side 'default' is only used when the ORM creates instances without explicit values; server_default is used when the DB inserts without the column.
issues.suggestion: Remove the duplicate 'default' where both are specified, keeping only server_default for the column-level default in the DB.

issues.description: Import 'json' is only used for json.loads on category_filter in the paper_trade_generation_loop (line 88). If the duplication is removed (as suggested), this import becomes unused.
issues.suggestion: Remove the json import if the category_filter duplication fix is applied.

issues.description: get_follow_info_for_embed makes 2 separate DB queries (one for the follow, one for category scores) that could be combined with a JOIN.
issues.suggestion: Use a single query with JOIN to fetch both follow info and category scores simultaneously.

issues.description: send_discord_alert creates a new httpx.AsyncClient per call. In the alert_delivery_loop in main.py, this means a new client per alert. Could reuse a shared client.
issues.suggestion: Create a shared httpx.AsyncClient and reuse it across calls.

issues.description: Mixes row-by-row iteration for upserts with accumulation dict for wallet_analytics update. Could use batch operations for the upsert instead of iterrows.
issues.suggestion: Consider using DataFrame.to_sql with method='multi' or a bulk insert pattern to avoid Python-level row iteration.

issues.description: Repeated use of float(row[...]) with None checks (lines 73-79) is verbose. A helper function like _safe_float used in the compute_category_follow_scores transformer would be cleaner.
issues.suggestion: Extract a reusable _safe_float helper, or reuse the one from compute_category_follow_scores.py via import.

issues.description: Builds a nested dict (category_scores_by_wallet) during the iteration loop, then uses it in a second loop. This is O(n) extra memory for the accumulation.
issues.suggestion: Use a defaultdict for cleaner accumulation: from collections import defaultdict; category_scores_by_wallet = defaultdict(dict)

issues.description: GLOBAL_METRICS_QUERY (50 lines) and CATEGORY_METRICS_QUERY (56 lines) are very long inline SQL strings. Makes the file hard to read and maintain.
issues.suggestion: Consider moving the SQL to separate .sql files in a queries/ directory or using SQLAlchemy's text() from imported modules.

issues.description: Two identical patterns for executing queries and converting to DataFrames. Could be factored into a helper function.
issues.suggestion: Extract a helper: def _query_to_df(conn, sql: str) -> DataFrame

issues.description: make_mock_db sets up a complex Mock hierarchy (mock_scalars, mock_result, etc.) that is duplicated for each test. Changes to the PaperPosition/PaperPortfolio model could silently break mocks.
issues.suggestion: Consider using a real test database or a lighter mocking approach like unittest.mock.patch for specific methods rather than building a full mock session.

issues.description: test_follow_duplicate asserts response.status_code in (201, 404, 409) - three possible outcomes depending on test execution order. This is a permissively flaky test that doesn't actually validate any specific behavior.
issues.suggestion: Set up explicit test data (create the wallet + follow relationship first) so the test can assert a specific expected status code.

issues.description: All 6 tests only check status codes, never validate response body content or schema. This is acceptable for a first pass but leaves gaps in coverage.
issues.suggestion: Add response body validation for at least the happy-path tests (test_reset_portfolio_empty should check that the returned portfolio has the expected balance).

issues.description: EMPTY_TABLES is set() suggesting no Phase 5 tables are expected to be empty. But there are no row threshold checks for any Phase 5 tables (wallet_follows, paper_portfolios, paper_positions, paper_trades, wallet_category_follow_scores). The tests just check that they're 'queryable' (COUNT >= 0 always passes).
issues.suggestion: Add minimum row thresholds for Phase 5 tables that are expected to have data (wallet_follows, wallet_category_follow_scores). Add paper_portfolios/paper_positions/paper_trades to EMPTY_TABLES if they're expected to be empty in production.

issues.description: Block 'trigger_follow_scoring' is wired into the orchestration pipeline between trigger_edge_scoring and trigger_verify. But the implementation (trigger_follow_scoring.py) is a no-op - it never calls trigger_pipeline('enrichment_follow_scoring', ...). This means the orchestration pipeline silently skips the entire enrichment_follow_scoring pipeline.
issues.suggestion: Implement trigger_follow_scoring.py to call trigger_pipeline('enrichment_follow_scoring', ...) following the pattern in trigger_edge_scoring.py, OR remove it from the orchestration pipeline if intentionally deferred.

issues.description: Block 'generate_paper_trades' is the final downstream block of 'export_alerts'. The implementation is a no-op (generate_paper_trades.py:21: pass). Paper trades are instead generated by the background service in app/main.py. This block adds pipeline overhead and confusion.
issues.suggestion: Remove the generate_paper_trades block from the smart_money_detection pipeline, or implement it for actual batch processing.

top_recommendations: 1. [HIGH] Fix trigger_follow_scoring.py — it's a no-op that silently skips the enrichment_follow_scoring pipeline in orchestration. Must call trigger_pipeline() like all other trigger_* exporters.

2. [HIGH] Extract duplicated formula weights into a shared module — service layer, ETL transformers, and unit tests all independently replicate the same scoring formulas (global: 0.30/0.20/0.20/0.15/0.15, category: 0.25/0.25/0.20/0.15/0.10/0.05). Weight changes will silently diverge.

3. [HIGH] Fix hardcoded volume_percentile=0.5 in follow_scoring.py:120 — the service layer's compute_category_follow_score ignores the actual volume_percentile while the ETL transformer uses it correctly. This produces different scores for the same wallet+category between the API and the DB.

4. [HIGH] Remove duplicated category_filter check in main.py:87-90 — the paper_trade_generation_loop redundantly checks category_filter before execute_copy_trade (paper_trading.py:21-24) already checks it. Remove the main.py version to eliminate the json.loads workaround for raw SQL.
5. [MEDIUM] Remove dead generate_paper_trades.py from smart_money_detection pipeline — it's an empty no-op that adds pipeline overhead. Either implement it or remove it.
